The gate is a bidirectional comparison of old and new representations: expected records, ordering and duplicate handling in both directions. Bounded sample checks, row counts or full-backup metadata cannot prove business equivalence.

Read authority may switch only when measured replication lag, completeness and read semantics meet owner-agreed thresholds; write authority only when rollback behavior and consistency across old and new clients are documented. Every intermediate configuration must have exactly one declared authoritative owner, and mixed-version compatibility must be demonstrated in both directions before authority moves.

An irreversible destructive migration needs explicit approval beyond successful code pull requests, plus a rehearsed recovery path: old binaries must interpret new persisted state, consumers must still accept the old contract, and new-only durable effects must be reconcilable before cleanup removes the old schema. Cutover is gated on operational evidence: verified replication health, a cleared dead-letter queue, data freshness at zero and an active reverse-replication fallback.

Equality is not correctness when both implementations share the same wrong semantics; a named business oracle is required, and happy-path-only comparisons are a refusal condition. Undefined identity mapping, unrecoverable writes or changed audit context are correct stops. A smaller reversible change or an additive mapping layer may be preferable. The sources establish no thresholds and record no executed cutover or restore.
